summary: In this opinion piece, Sam Altman argues that the human-machine merge has already begun and will be gradual rather than a singular event. He warns that AI and related technologies are advancing exponentially, making the merge happen sooner than expected, and calls for urgent worldwide coordination. He also reflects on the personal and societal dangers of attention-hacking algorithms.

claims.text: Altman believes the merge of humans and machines has already started and is a few years in.
claims.evidence_quote: I believe the merge has already started, and we are a few years in.

claims.text: Guesses for when humans and machines merge range from 2025 to 2075.
claims.evidence_quote: Most guesses seem to be between 2025 and 2075.

claims.text: The word 'singularity' is now avoided by many because it feels uncomfortable and real.
claims.evidence_quote: now it feels uncomfortable and real enough that many seem to avoid naming it at all.

claims.text: Phones, social media feeds, and search engines already control, determine, and decide human behavior.
claims.evidence_quote: Our phones control us and tell us what to do when; social media feeds determine how we feel; search engines decide what we think.

claims.text: Altman says the algorithms behind these systems are no longer understood by any one person.
claims.evidence_quote: The algorithms that make all this happen are no longer understood by any one person.

claims.text: Altman describes his own addiction to the internet and the effort needed to resist the algorithms.
claims.evidence_quote: Until I made a real effort to combat it, I found myself getting extremely addicted to the internet.

claims.text: Altman says the merge is already in a co-evolution phase where AIs affect us and we improve the AI.
claims.evidence_quote: We are already in the phase of co-evolution — the AIs affect, effect, and infect us, and then we improve the AI.

claims.text: Altman states that superhuman AI, genetic enhancement, and brain-machine interfaces are going to happen unless we destroy ourselves first.
claims.evidence_quote: More important than that, unless we destroy ourselves first, superhuman AI is going to happen, genetic enhancement is going to happen, and brain-machine interfaces are going to happen.

claims.text: Altman thinks a human-machine merge is probably the best-case scenario for avoiding conflict between species.
claims.evidence_quote: But I think a merge is probably our best-case scenario.

claims.text: Humans will be the first species ever to design their own descendants.
claims.evidence_quote: We will be the first species ever to design our own descendants.

claims.text: Altman says hardware is improving exponentially and the number of smart people working on AI is increasing exponentially, so the merge will likely happen sooner than expected.
claims.evidence_quote: Hardware is improving at an exponential rate—the most surprising thing I’ve learned working on OpenAI is just how correlated increasing computing power and AI breakthroughs are—and the number of smart people working on AI is increasing exponentially as well.

claims.text: Altman calls on the world to take AI seriously now because worldwide coordination is slow.
claims.evidence_quote: It would be good for the entire world to start taking this a lot more seriously now. Worldwide coordination doesn’t happen quickly, and we need it for this.

claims.text: Altman predicts attention hacking will be the sugar epidemic of this generation.
claims.evidence_quote: I believe attention hacking is going to be the sugar epidemic of this generation.
